transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this review session. As you know, we have a student who was below the college's academic-standing standard and has submitted a draft academic recovery contract for the spring term. Before I can approve and sign off on the final contract, I need to make sure we've addressed all the required elements: the student's enrollment plan, any conditions for continued enrollment, and the support services that will be monitored. The student has also asked to return to regular enrollment after the spring term, so we should consider whether the draft plan adequately supports that transition. I'd like to hear from each of you — what information do you have that's relevant to finalizing this contract?

commitments.detail: Revise the draft enrollment plan to replace the listed elective with CHEM 201 (4 credits), the only approved course for repairing the failed major requirement.
Enter into the contract template the condition that the student must complete 12 credits during the spring term for academic-standing reinstatement.
Add to the contract the condition that at least 6 of the 12 required credits must be delivered asynchronously, based on the student's documented caregiving obligation.
Attach to the contract the financial-aid requirement that the student meet with their advisor every two weeks for the first 8 weeks of the term.
Once all four conditions and the corrected enrollment plan are incorporated into the contract, compile the final version for Dr. Morgan's review and signoff.
